title: Break and Continue
description: Stop a loop early with break, or skip one turn with continue.

items.sub: Skips the rest of this turn and moves on to the next one.

content.title: Normally a loop runs every turn. Two keywords change that.

content.real: A lift going up a building
content.text: `break` is getting out and leaving the building: no more floors. `continue` is skipping one floor: the lift still carries on to the top.

content.value: Both usually sit inside an `if`, so they only happen in the case you care about. They are easy to mix up, so the widget below runs the same loop with each one. Switch between them and watch the trace change.

content.question: Which keyword ends the whole loop right away?
content.explain: `break` leaves the loop entirely. `continue` only skips the rest of one turn.

items: As soon as Python reaches `break`, it leaves the loop entirely.
The turns that were still to come never happen at all.

steps.note: `break`: leave the loop now. `print(n)` is skipped, and turn 4 never happens.

content.title: Watch break end the loop
content.outro: Only 1 and 2 were printed. `n` never reached 4.

output: Stop! Something is wrong with cookie 4.
content.caption: Cookies 1, 2 and 3 get eaten. The break on cookie 4 stops the loop, so cookie 5 is never reached.

content.question: What is the last number this prints?
content.explain: When `n` is 3 the `break` runs before `print`, so the loop ends. The last number printed was 2.

items: It jumps straight to the next turn, skipping whatever was left in this one.
The loop still runs to the end. One turn just does less work.

steps.note: `continue`: skip the rest of this turn. `print(n)` does not run for 3.
The loop does NOT end. Turn 4: `n` is `4`.
`range(1, 5)` has no numbers left, so the loop ends normally.

content.title: Watch continue skip a turn
content.outro: 1, 2 and 4 were printed. Only 3 was skipped.

items.title: break
items.text: Prints `1` and `2`. The loop ends at 3.

items.title: continue

content.caption: Floors 1, 2, 4 and 5 are visited. Floor 3 is skipped, but the lift still carries on to the top.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: When `n` is 2, `continue` skips the `print` for that turn only. The loop carries on, so 1 and 3 are printed.

practice.question: Change the code to print the numbers 1 to 5 but skip the number 3. Replace pass with the right keyword.
Make this loop stop completely once it reaches 4, so it only prints 1, 2 and 3.

quiz.question: Which keyword stops the whole loop right away?
quiz.explain: break leaves the loop completely. continue only skips one turn, and pass does nothing at all.

quiz.question: What does 'continue' do inside a loop?
options: Skips the rest of this turn and starts the next one.
Starts the loop again from the beginning.
quiz.explain: continue skips whatever is left in the current turn and jumps to the next one. The loop itself keeps going.

quiz.question: What does this print?  for i in range(1, 5):  /  if i == 2: continue  /  print(i)
quiz.explain: continue skips only the turn where i is 2. Every other turn prints as normal, so you get 1, 3, 4.
